stis_g430l.source_kind: Gaussian FWHM reduction of tabulated model point-source LSFs
stis_g430l.source_definition: Relative pixel offset and model LSF amplitudes for four apertures; select 52x2.0 (column 5). Not empirical in-flight LSF measurements. Original amplitudes and asymmetric wings are not redistributed as Gaussian kernels.
stis_g430l.calibration_identifier: Unversioned STScI model LSF text files; spectral-resolution page last updated 2023-06-02; source bytes pinned by SHA-256
stis_g430l.processing: Find the two half-maximum crossings surrounding the maximum of the unnormalized 52x2.0 LSF using linear interpolation in pixel offset. Do not fit a Gaussian or use a second moment. Interpolate FWHM in wavelength between available LSF and handbook anchors; hold endpoint FWHMs outside the anchors, including convolution padding. Multiply by the average grating dispersion and sample R; runtime linearly interpolates R without extrapolation.
stis_g430l.boundary_assumption: Endpoint FWHM extension is a Speclib nominal approximation, not additional LSF calibration. G430L interpolates between its two downloadable LSF wavelengths.
stis_g430l.model_pedigree_note: The STIS handbook states that internal-lamp and on-orbit observations confirmed and revised the original pre-flight model LSFs. The downloaded text files do not identify their individual model revision or a calibration release version. Differences from handbook FWHMs are retained; their cause is not established by the unversioned source files.

wfc3_g102.source_kind: Nominal analytic approximation anchored to handbook resolving power
wfc3_g102.source_definition: Table 8.1 resolving power uses the FWHM of the Gaussian image core measured perpendicular to dispersion; mean IR grism dispersion is in nm/pixel (field center for G102). Not a measured wavelength-dependent LSF.
wfc3_g102.calibration_identifier: WFC3 Instrument Handbook Table 8.1, Cycle 34 online snapshot retrieved 2026-10-20; no separate calibration release version
wfc3_g102.equation: R(lambda) = R_reference * lambda_um / reference_wavelength_um; constant delta_lambda = reference_wavelength_um/R_reference
wfc3_g102.processing: Adopt the published reference resolving power exactly and hold its wavelength FWHM constant. The effective pixel FWHM is (1000*reference_wavelength_um/R_reference)/dispersion_nm_per_pixel, not an imposed two-pixel width. Sample the linear R prescription at the two domain endpoints; runtime linear interpolation is exact for this prescription.

niriss_soss_order1.institution: Albert et al.; NIRISS/SOSS instrument team (Universite de Montreal, STScI, NRC and collaborators)
niriss_soss_order1.source_kind: Nominal analytic approximation from order-specific CV3 dispersion and two-pixel resolution convention
niriss_soss_order1.source_definition: Albert et al. (2023), Table 2 and Section 5.3/Figure 7: CV3-measured average order dispersion (about +/-2%) with a two-pixel Nyquist resolution element. This is not a measured in-flight Gaussian LSF; Figure 6 individual LED widths vary from 1.8 to 2.6 pixels.
niriss_soss_order1.calibration_identifier: Albert et al. (2023), PASP 135, 075001, Table 2 and Section 5.3; calibration-status review 2026-10-20
niriss_soss_order1.coverage_note: Order 1 uses rounded JDox useful coverage 0.9-2.8 um. Order 2 is restricted by Speclib to 0.6-1.0 um following the calibration-status page (updated 2026-06-22), which advises against using the low-signal region above 1 um. Wider geometric coverage is not claimed as useful output.
niriss_soss_order1.processing: Use the measured Table 2 dispersion for this order (not the parenthesized optical-model value) and two pixels per resolution element. Hold the average dispersion constant, yielding wavelength-dependent R. This approximates the optical-model/derivative curve; do not digitize Figure 7 or claim to reproduce a visit-specific wavelength solution. Adopt the resolution element as Gaussian FWHM; sample the linear equation at the two padding-domain endpoints.
